instrumentDesign.where: services/retrieval-api/src/ledger-serving-measure.ts (pure logic + the SQL builders), src/__tests__/ledger-serving-measure.test.ts (self-tests), scripts/ledger-serving-measure.mjs (the driver, run through tsx, same convention as the repo's run-bastrop-spine-health.mjs)
instrumentDesign.whyBesideTheReader: Every measurement here is a question about the shape parcel-record-reader.ts consumes. Its extractAtomDid (parcel-record-reader.ts:63-67, and the comment above it: 'P-163 has not landed; no live cell carries one yet') reads exactly ONE field, top-level cell.atomDid. Keeping the pointer vocabulary next to the reader means the next pointer field is grep-adjacent to its reader.

pointerVocabulary.whyNamedNotImplied: A measurement that tested only atomDid would report '0 of 26,814,129' and could not tell a reader that is unprepared from a writer that used a different spelling. The candidate list closes that for the FULL population; the sampled key vocabulary closes it for arbitrary spellings on a 378-parcel sample.
pointerVocabulary.nestedPointersExcluded: A nested pointer (an inputs[].atomDid) is NOT counted, because extractAtomDid would not follow it either. Counting it would report a readiness the serve path does not have.
pointerVocabulary.nullAndBlankExcluded: atomDid: null or whitespace is not a reference. Without this the two claims '0 carry a pointer' and '0 carry a pointer I recognise' are the same observation.

instrumentDesign.countingRule: A 'value' cell splits into value-with-pointer and value-copied-only; a value cell with no scalar `value` is its own state; non-value kinds keep their own names. The split is ONE function (shapeKindOf) so a SQL FILTER cannot drift from what the reader does.
instrumentDesign.sqlGuards: Every emitted statement carries SET statement_timeout and SET default_transaction_read_only=on in the statement itself, never as a caller's habit; countyFips and parcelNodeId are shape-checked before any SQL string is built; the atoms lookup refuses an empty id list so a whole-table query cannot be emitted by this instrument.
instrumentDesign.selfTestDirections: The committed test asserts both directions on the SAME function the live run calls: a cell with a reference reports it, and the live cell shape (48209:100226's setbackFrontFt cell_state, read 2026-09-16) reports none. It also asserts non-vacuity (null/blank pointer does not count), that the SQL's array literal equals the TypeScript vocabulary (so the two cannot drift), that the CSV header assertion can fail, and that cold and warm samples are never pooled.

m1.question: For every one of the 65 rails across the six counties: how many value cells carry an atom reference of any kind, how many carry only a copied value, and which writer wrote them.
m1.accessPath: SELECT rail_key, coalesce(cell_state->>'kind','(no-kind)'), coalesce(cell_state->>'source','(no-source)'), (cell_state ?| array[...pointer vocab...]), count(*) FROM parcel_record_cell WHERE place_key >= '<fips>:' AND place_key < '<fips+1>:' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 — one statement per county, the county place_key prefix range on the (place_key, rail_key) primary key. Relational comparison: 'is the cell count per county 65 x parcels?' is the completeness check, so a partial scan cannot look like an absence.
m1.heavyScan: Announced before running: factory store, six counties, ~90-330 s per county, statement_timeout 1500 s embedded.

m2.question: For the setback and envelope rails, do atoms exist in the atoms store for those parcels and values, and do the atom's own values agree with the cell's copied values?
m2.catalogFirst: Starting from pg_indexes: atoms has atoms_pkey (atom_did), atoms_entity_type_idx (entity_type), atoms_jurisdiction_idx, atoms_entity_composite_unique (entity_type, entity_id) UNIQUE, atoms_property_parcel_node_idx (body->>'parcelNodeId', partial, for zoning-fact/setback-rule/buildable-envelope/parcel-terrain-model), atoms_boundary_parcel_node_idx, atoms_road_node_id_idx, atoms_road_county_fips_idx, atoms_parcel_node_lookup_idx, atoms_section_number_partial_idx, atoms_parcel_node_county_idx, atoms_building_footprint_parcel_node_idx. entity_type has 18 distinct values (pg_stats most_common_vals), including setback-rule, zoning-fact, buildable-envelope, parcel-terrain-model.
m2.chosenPath: (entity_type, entity_id) — atoms_entity_composite_unique — because entity_id IS the parcelNodeId for these entity types (verified live: entity_id '48209:100226' is also body->>'parcelNodeId'). N point lookups, never a scan.
m2.sample: Parcels drawn from parcel_record_cell itself, stratified by city (the zoningJurisdictionKey rail's value), up to 20-25 per city, targeting >= 50 per county: 48021 60, 48055 80, 48209 80, 48309 50, 48453 54, 48491 54 = 378.
m2.plans: EXPLAIN (never ANALYZE) for BOTH spellings, pasted in CP2.

falsifierAnswersPreRegistered.f1: The instrument reports a pointer cell and a non-pointer cell correctly, both directions. PREDICTED: PASS. The two directions are the committed test's first two cases, and the live measurement's negative case is the REAL live shape (26,814,129 value cells, 0 with a pointer), so the negative direction is not synthetic. Proven by running the test, and by the live run agreeing with the fixture on the same classification function.
falsifierAnswersPreRegistered.f2: The atoms query plan uses an index. PREDICTED: PASS for the (entity_type, entity_id) spelling (Index Scan on atoms_entity_composite_unique, cost 0.69..8.71) and FAIL-BY-DESIGN for the body->>'parcelNodeId' spelling (BitmapAnd of the partial index with atoms_entity_type_idx, cost 10143.38..11021.14, and it estimates 31,591 rows for ONE parcelNodeId). The measured path is the first, and the second is reported because it is the spell a builder would reach for by intuition and it is ~1,400x the cost estimate.
falsifierAnswersPreRegistered.f3: The /record timing covers at least three counties. PREDICTED: PASS at four (48021, 48309, 48453, 48491), 5 parcels each.
falsifierAnswersPreRegistered.preRegisteredTrap: PREDICTED BEFORE MEASURING, and it is the reason this lane exists: 0 of the value cells carry a pointer, so a ledger-served surface today would have to read the COPIED value, not dereference an atom — and for the setback rails the atoms that do exist will disagree with the copied values on a material fraction of parcels. Both predictions are stated here so the CP2 numbers can be checked against them rather than narrated.

notChanging: No store write, no atom mint, no migration, no reader or writer edit (parcel-record-db.ts and parcel-record-reader.ts are untouched).
No deploy; the Cloud Run revision was read, never written.
Nothing outside services/retrieval-api/ in the engine clone; the factory, LDT and hauska-map trees are read-only inputs.
The PR carries the instrument and its self-tests only — no probe harness, no measurement output, no close artifacts.
openRisks: M2's atom-existence answer is a SAMPLE (378 parcels, >=50 per county) and is reported with its denominator. Its per-county spread is large (setback atom coverage 0/50 in McLennan vs 40/60 in Bastrop), so the county-level numbers must not be read as statewide rates.

The uncomparable case (atom exists, no comparable front value) is measured but is not the same thing as a stale atom: no fetched_at comparison is made between the cell and its atom in this lane, so the disagreement count is a disagreement count, not a prove of which side is newer.

The /record route is timed on the DEPLOYED revision, which serves the factory store and does not dereference atoms today (no pointer exists to dereference). The timing therefore answers 'what a cold read costs now', not 'what it will cost once cells carry pointers'.

One unindexed ORDER BY fetched_at query against the 199 GB atoms table was launched by mistake during reconnaissance and killed within ~35 s; it is disclosed in CP2 with what it did and did not do. No other scan in this lane ran without a statement_timeout.

The Travis county sample (48453) took 268 s and McLennan 81 s for the same shape of statement - the county place_key prefix range does not have a uniform cost per row. Recorded as a fact for whoever designs the cut-over, because a per-parcel direct read is a different cost question.
